Mobile commerce · Redesign concept

Levi’s

A clearer path from discovery to denim.

A mobile app redesign concept that brings structure to product discovery, search, favorites, and checkout while retaining the character of an established brand.

Format
Mobile app
Focus
UX analysis, interaction design, visual design
01 Overview02 Decisions03 Design04 Reflection

01 / The context

The experience behind the screens.

Shopping should make it easy to find the right product and understand the next step. In the Levi’s India app, I identified opportunities to simplify navigation, improve product information, and make saved items easier to revisit. This concept follows the shopping journey from the home screen to the cart.

The design challenge

Promotional banners dominated the home screen. Product categories required repeated navigation, while long descriptions pushed useful choices further down the product page. Favorites and cart controls also needed a clearer hierarchy.

02 / Design decisions

What shaped
the experience.

01

Give discovery a starting point

Bring search to the top, group promotions into a carousel, and create clear sections for featured categories and new arrivals.

02

Make the next choice easier

Use expandable category menus, recent searches, and suggestions. Organize favorites by product category so saved items are easier to scan.

03

Bring buying information together

Reorder product details around price, color, size, reviews, and shipping. Add a cart progression indicator and simplify promotional-code entry.

04 / Reflection

What this
work brings together.

The result is a connected set of redesigned shopping screens with an explicit link between each usability issue and the proposed change. A useful next validation step would be to compare product-finding and cart-editing tasks with shoppers.
